biome.name: Biome
biome.summary: Combined linter and formatter for JavaScript and TypeScript in a single fast Rust binary.
biome.problem: Running a linter and a formatter as two separate tools means two configs to keep in sync and two passes over every file, until something merges them into one.
benefits: Lints and formats JS/TS in one tool instead of maintaining ESLint and Prettier configs side by side
Runs as a single native binary, so checks and formatting stay fast even on large repos

codeql.name: CodeQL
codeql.summary: GitHub's own semantic code analysis engine, built into code scanning to find security vulnerabilities.
codeql.problem: A vulnerability that only shows up through the way tainted data flows across functions and files ships unnoticed because nothing traces execution paths through the code, only individual lines or patterns.
benefits: Models source code as a queryable database, so it traces tainted data across functions and files rather than matching single lines
Runs as part of GitHub code scanning, surfacing results as pull request checks and Security tab alerts with no separate dashboard to run
Maintained and updated by GitHub, with standard query packs covering major languages out of the box

dependabot.name: Dependabot
dependabot.summary: GitHub's native dependency update bot, enabled by committing a config file instead of running a service.
dependabot.problem: Dependencies quietly drift out of date and known-vulnerable versions sit unpatched, unless something opens the update PRs on its own.
benefits: Opens version and security update PRs on a schedule, with no service to host or run
Ships as a native GitHub feature, so one config file is the entire setup

eslint.name: ESLint
eslint.summary: Static analysis for JavaScript and TypeScript, driven by a flat config the repo owns.
eslint.problem: Inconsistent JS/TS style and easy mistakes like unused variables pile up across a repo without an enforced linter.
benefits: Enforces one JS/TS style across a repo instead of relying on review comments
Catches common bugs (unused variables, unreachable code) before they reach review

gitleaks.name: Gitleaks
gitleaks.summary: Open source secret scanner that matches git history, diffs, and working-tree files against a regex-based detection ruleset.
gitleaks.problem: A credential typed into a commit sits in the repository the moment it's pushed, with nothing in CI to catch it before it merges.
benefits: Scans full git history and diffs for hardcoded secrets, not just the current working tree
Runs as a CLI, pre-commit hook, or GitHub Action to catch a leak before it merges
Supports custom and extended TOML rule configs for org-specific secret patterns

go-test.name: go test
go-test.summary: The Go toolchain's built-in test runner, with coverage instrumentation included at no extra install.
go-test.problem: Regressions in Go code ship unnoticed because nothing runs the package's tests, even though the runner is already sitting in the toolchain.
benefits: Runs unit tests and reports line coverage from the same command, no extra dependency
Ships with every Go install, so there is no version to pin or tool to vendor

golangci-lint.name: golangci-lint
golangci-lint.summary: Fast Go linters runner that bundles staticcheck, go vet, and dozens of other linters behind one config.
golangci-lint.problem: Style drift and bug patterns like ignored errors or vet failures pile up across a Go repo without an enforced linter running them all in one pass.
benefits: Runs staticcheck, go vet, and dozens of other Go linters together, so a separate static-analysis tool isn't needed
Enforces one Go style and lint ruleset across a repo instead of relying on review comments
Runs the same linters locally and in CI through one config file

hadolint.name: hadolint
hadolint.summary: Dockerfile linter checked against a ruleset baked into its own binary.
hadolint.problem: A Dockerfile with an unpinned base image or a risky instruction ships unnoticed without a linter checking it.
benefits: Catches Dockerfile anti-patterns (unpinned base images, misplaced ADD/COPY) before build
Enforces one consistent Dockerfile style across every repo that runs it

blocking.note: Dockerfile lint findings can fail the aggregate gate and merge.

jacoco.name: JaCoCo
jacoco.summary: Code coverage instrumentation and reporting for JVM projects.
jacoco.problem: A test suite exists and passes, but without coverage instrumentation nobody actually knows how much of the codebase it exercises.
benefits: Shows which lines and branches tests actually exercise, not just whether the suite passes
Lets a build fail on a coverage drop instead of relying on someone noticing later

jest.name: Jest
jest.summary: The incumbent batteries-included JS/TS test runner, bundling assertions, mocking, and coverage in one tool - a solid alternative to Vitest, not a new default over it.
jest.problem: Regressions in JS/TS logic ship silently and coverage goes unmeasured, unless a test runner actually executes the unit tests and reports on them.
benefits: Runs unit tests, mocking, and coverage from one dependency, with no separate assertion library needed
Long-established with broad framework support and a large ecosystem of transforms and matchers

junit.name: JUnit
junit.summary: The standard unit testing framework for the JVM, built on the Jupiter programming model.
junit.problem: Broken logic in JVM code compiles cleanly and passes review, then only surfaces once it runs in production, unless something exercises it first.
benefits: Catches logic regressions locally, before they reach code review or production
Gives every build a repeatable pass/fail signal instead of manual verification

kingfisher.name: Kingfisher
kingfisher.summary: Secrets scanner for git history and working trees.
kingfisher.problem: A secret committed to git stays recoverable from history forever, even after the file that held it is deleted.
benefits: Finds secrets already committed to git history, not just the working tree
Blocks a new commit from introducing a live credential or API key

secrets_exclude_file.note: Path to a file listing secret-scan patterns you want to exclude (e.g. known test fixtures), if any.

azure_tenant_id.note: Which Azure AD tenant that app lives in.

azure_subscription_id.note: Which Azure subscription owns the image registry.

playwright.name: Playwright
playwright.summary: End-to-end browser testing framework that drives real Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit engines from a single config.
playwright.problem: A broken user flow across pages or browsers reaches production because unit tests exercise functions, not the browser a real user clicks through.
benefits: Runs real user flows in actual browser engines, not just unit-level assertions
Catches cross-browser and multi-page regressions before they reach users
Auto-waits for elements and network calls, cutting the flaky failures common in browser automation

prettier.name: Prettier
prettier.summary: Opinionated code formatter for JavaScript, TypeScript, and related web formats.
prettier.problem: Formatting drifts across a codebase and reviewers spend time on spacing and line-break comments instead of substance, unless a formatter enforces one style automatically.
benefits: Enforces one formatting style across a repo without manual review comments
Formats on save or in CI, so style never becomes a discussion topic

pytest.name: pytest
pytest.summary: Test framework for writing and running Python unit tests, with coverage via the pytest-cov plugin.
pytest.problem: Regressions in Python code slip past review and ship because nothing runs the test suite or reports which lines it never touched.
benefits: Runs Python unit tests with plain assert statements and fixtures, no boilerplate test classes required
Measures test coverage via the pytest-cov plugin, showing exactly which lines and branches ran

renovate.name: Renovate
renovate.summary: Automated dependency update bot that opens PRs to keep versions current across languages and package managers.
renovate.problem: Dependency versions quietly fall behind upstream, and a fix for a known vulnerability sits unmerged for weeks, unless something opens the update itself.
benefits: Opens dependency update PRs automatically across dozens of package managers and languages
Runs as a hosted GitHub App with no config, or self-hosted via the open source CLI for full control
Groups and schedules updates so a repo isn't flooded with one PR per dependency bump

ruff.name: Ruff
ruff.summary: Fast Python linter and formatter, covering both style/bug checks and code formatting in one tool.
ruff.problem: Inconsistent Python style and unused imports pile up across a repo, and formatting drifts between contributors, without a single enforced linter and formatter.
benefits: Lints and formats Python in one pass, at a speed that keeps it usable on every commit
Its format subcommand is Black-compatible, which is why there's no separate Black entry in this catalogue
Replaces a stack of older tools (Flake8, isort, pyupgrade) with one config surface

semgrep.name: Semgrep
semgrep.summary: Static analysis scanner for security and correctness rules across languages.
semgrep.problem: A security or correctness bug that matches a known-bad pattern reaches production because nothing checks for the pattern, only the types.
benefits: Finds security and correctness bugs from pattern rules, across languages, without a full type-checked build
Runs the same ruleset locally and in CI, so a finding never surprises a reviewer

spotbugs.name: SpotBugs
spotbugs.summary: Bytecode-level static analysis for JVM projects.
spotbugs.problem: Bug patterns like null dereferences and resource leaks compile cleanly and only surface at runtime, unless something inspects the bytecode first.
benefits: Finds real bug patterns (null dereferences, resource leaks) that compile cleanly but fail at runtime
Runs against compiled bytecode, so it catches issues style linters that only read source miss

trivy.name: Trivy
trivy.summary: Filesystem, image, and IaC vulnerability scanner.
trivy.problem: Vulnerable dependencies and misconfigured infrastructure reach production when nothing scans for them before merge.
benefits: Flags known-vulnerable dependencies before they reach a release
Catches misconfigured cloud resources in Terraform/CloudFormation before merge
Blocks a vulnerable base image from shipping in a container build

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.summary: Compile-time type checking for JavaScript and TypeScript codebases.
typescript.problem: A type mismatch between what a function expects and what it's actually passed compiles cleanly and ships, because tests only exercise the paths they cover, not every call site's types.
benefits: Catches type mismatches at compile time, before they reach tests or production
Checks every call site's types, not just the paths tests happen to exercise

vitest.name: Vitest
vitest.summary: Vite-native unit test runner for JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
vitest.problem: Regressions ship silently between releases when a repo has no enforced automated test suite to catch them first.
benefits: Runs unit tests against Vite's own transform pipeline, so no separate build step is needed
Produces coverage reports that show untested code paths before they reach production

ci-base-checks.name: Korza CI Base Checks
ci-base-checks.summary: One container image wrapping the mandatory secrets, SAST, SCA, IaC, and Dockerfile checks for every Korza pipeline.
ci-base-checks.problem: Without a shared checks image, every repo re-implements its own secrets, SAST, SCA, IaC, and Dockerfile scanning - inconsistently, and often not at all.
benefits: One image covers secrets, SAST, SCA, IaC, and Dockerfile checks with no separate tool setup
Upgrades to the underlying tools roll out without any consumer changing their workflow
One consistent set of blocking rules across every Korza pipeline
